question: How many times was a Twitter/X post cited as a reference on the english Wikipedia pages for each day of August in the last June 2023 versions of the pages?

history.name: Citation_Expert
history.content:
Task setup and plan:
- Goal: Count how many times a Twitter/X post was cited as a reference on the English Wikipedia pages for each day of August (pages: "August 1" ... "August 31"), using the last June 2023 versions of those pages.
- Approach (no full dump needed):
  1) Use MediaWiki API to retrieve the revision for each page as of 2023-06-30T23:59:59Z (the last June 2023 snapshot).
  2) Parse the wikitext references (<ref>...</ref>) for URLs referencing twitter.com or x.com, including archived versions pointing to twitter URLs.
  3) Also scan for cite tweet templates if present.
  4) Count per page, then sum if needed.
- I will prepare a Python script to:
  - Iterate pages ["August 1", ..., "August 31"].
  - Fetch revision <= 2023-06-30 23:59:59 (UTC) with action=query&prop=revisions&rvprop=content|timestamp&rvdir=older&rvstart=2023-06-30T23:59:59Z&rvlimit=1.
  - Extract references and count Twitter/X citations.
Request: Computer_terminal ready to run Python when provided.

history.name: Wikipedia_Citation_Expert
history.content:
Definition and extraction criteria for Twitter/X citations on day-of-August pages:
- Include references that contain URLs to specific tweets:
  - twitter.com/*/status/* (including mobile.twitter.com)
  - x.com/*/status/*
  - Archived URLs (web.archive.org, archive.today) whose original URL is a twitter.com/*/status/* or x.com/*/status/*
- Include cite tweet templates ({{cite tweet}} and {{tweet}}) if present, as they imply a tweet citation even if url is not explicit.
- Exclude user profiles, lists, search pages (no /status/ path), and embeds without identifiable post.
- No need to determine the tweet’s original posting date; we just count presence of tweet citations in the page references.
- We must ensure we use the last June 2023 revision of each day page.
Regex heuristics:
- Raw URLs: r"https?://(mobile\.)?(twitter\.com|x\.com)/[^\s\|\}<>]*/status/\d+"
- Archived: r"https?://web\.archive\.org/web/\d+/(https?://(mobile\.)?(twitter\.com|x\.com)/[^\s\|\}<>]*/status/\d+)" and similar for archive.*
- Templates: detect {{cite tweet}} or {{tweet}} in references.

history.name: Citation_Expert
history.content:
Providing Python script to fetch last June 2023 revision and count Twitter/X citations per page.

Python (requests + mw API + regex):

import re, requests
from urllib.parse import quote

SESSION = requests.Session()
API = "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"
CUTOFF = "2023-06-30T23:59:59Z"

PAGES = [f"August {i}" for i in range(1, 32)]

re_tweet = re.compile(r"https?://(mobile\.)?(twitter\.com|x\.com)/[^\s\|\}<>]*/status/\d+", re.I)
re_arch = re.compile(r"https?://web\.archive\.org/web/\d+/(https?://(mobile\.)?(twitter\.com|x\.com)/[^\s\|\}<>]*/status/\d+)", re.I)
re_cite_tweet = re.compile(r"\{\{\s*(cite tweet|tweet)\b", re.I)


def fetch_rev_wikitext(title):
    params = {
        "action": "query",
        "prop": "revisions",
        "titles": title,
        "rvprop": "content|timestamp",
        "rvslots": "main",
        "rvdir": "older",
        "rvstart": CUTOFF,
        "rvlimit": 1,
        "format": "json",
        "formatversion": 2,
    }
    r = SESSION.get(API, params=params, timeout=30)
    r.raise_for_status()
    data = r.json()
    pages = data.get("query", {}).get("pages", [])
    if not pages or "revisions" not in pages[0]:
        return None, None
    rev = pages[0]["revisions"][0]
    ts = rev.get("timestamp")
    content = rev.get("slots", {}).get("main", {}).get("content", "")
    return ts, content


def count_twitter_refs(wikitext):
    # naive split on <ref ...> ... </ref>
    refs = re.findall(r"<ref[>\s][\s\S]*?</ref>", wikitext, re.I)
    count = 0
    for ref in refs:
        if re_tweet.search(ref) or re_arch.search(ref) or re_cite_tweet.search(ref):
            count += 1
    return count

results = {}
for title in PAGES:
    ts, text = fetch_rev_wikitext(title)
    if text is None:
        results[title] = {"count": 0, "timestamp": None}
        continue
    c = count_twitter_refs(text)
    results[title] = {"count": c, "timestamp": ts}

print("SUMMARY_COUNTS:")
for t in PAGES:
    r = results[t]
    print(f"{t}: {r['count']} (rev {r['timestamp']})")

total = sum(r["count"] for r in results.values())
print("TOTAL_TWITTER_CITES:", total)

Please execute this script.
